title: Behaviour-Based Temperature-Sensor Role Inference and Lagged Weight-Gain Event Prediction in Multi-Year Smart-Hive Telemetry
content: Long-term smart-hive datasets are difficult to interpret because nominally identical temperature channels may represent different physical positions, while hive weight integrates biological activity, management and technical artefacts. We analysed BeeHUB telemetry collected from 4 January 2022 to 2 December 2025 to infer temperature-channel roles and evaluate strictly lagged prediction of an operational weight-gain event. The role-corrected active-season dataset contained 35,332 hive-days from 110 hives, of which 27,756 were weather matched. Role inference used thermal offset, daily range and ambient correlation, with at least eight concurrent hourly observations required per audit day. The event was daytime weight gain of at least 0.3 kg and was not treated as validated nectar-flow ground truth. During main flow, warm-stable hive-days showed a median inferred internal temperature of 34.8 ◦C, thermal buffer of 17.0 ◦C, daytime gain of 0.35 kg and event rate of 52.5%. Positive contrasts persisted after outside-temperature stratification, within-hive comparison and repeated hive subsampling. On fixed unseen-hive splits, the all-history histogram-gradient-boosting classifier achieved ROC AUC 0.799 in main flow and 0.820 in summer. These results support behaviour-based sensor-role inference and separation of biological context from autoregressive operational prediction.
